questions.q: What does AWS Organizations govern, as distinct from Azure Policy (Lesson 18)?
options: Individual S3 objects only
Only billing, never access control
Entire AWS accounts, grouped into organizational units, rather than individual resources
The exact same scope as Azure Policy, just with different terminology
questions.explain: AWS Organizations operates at the account level — grouping whole accounts into OUs — while Azure Policy evaluates individual resources.

questions.q: What is a service control policy (SCP), fundamentally?
options: An IAM policy that directly grants permissions to users
A billing policy that controls spending limits
A resource tag used for cost allocation
A permission ceiling that sets the maximum available permissions for IAM users and roles in covered accounts — it never grants anything by itself
questions.explain: An SCP is a ceiling, not a grant — it can only narrow what IAM policies in the account are allowed to permit, never add permissions on its own.

questions.q: Which accounts does a service control policy NEVER apply to?
options: Accounts created in the last 30 days
Any account in a child OU
The organization's management account
Any account with the default FullAWSAccess policy attached
questions.explain: SCPs apply only to member accounts — the management account is explicitly excluded from SCP enforcement.

questions.q: If an account's OU has no SCPs beyond the default, but a parent OU above it has a Deny SCP attached, is the account restricted?
options: Only if the SCP is manually re-attached to every child OU
Yes — the effective permission ceiling is the intersection of every SCP that applies, including ones inherited from parent OUs
Only if the account is the management account
No — only SCPs attached directly to an account's own OU ever apply
questions.explain: SCPs combine down the hierarchy — an account's effective ceiling includes every SCP from its own OU plus every OU above it up to the root.

questions.q: In the lesson's example SCP denying CloudTrail actions, what can an IAM policy in a covered account do about that deny?
options: Only the root user can bypass the SCP
Nothing — no IAM policy can override an SCP's explicit deny, no matter how permissive it is
IAM policies and SCPs don't interact at all
An IAM policy with AdministratorAccess can always override an SCP
questions.explain: SCPs set a hard ceiling — an explicit deny in an SCP cannot be overridden by any IAM policy in the accounts it covers.
